metadata.title: MIMIC four-patient graph schema
metadata.format: Descriptive graph contract with table context.

graph_document_fields.metadata: Graph identity, dataset, patient scope, provenance, table labels, join definitions and counts.
graph_document_fields.nodes: Array conforming to node_common_fields and node_types.
graph_document_fields.relations: Array conforming to relation_common_fields and relations.

node_common_fields.id: Unique string: mimic-iv-demo:<version>:<source_table>:<source_row>; identifies one original CSV data record.
node_common_fields.type: One of the 12 node_types; used as the Neo4j entity label.
node_common_fields.name: Derived display string; may repeat. Diagnosis/Procedure use linked long_title; LabEvent uses its LabItem label.
node_common_fields.properties: Object with every source field listed in node_types[type].properties plus node_common_properties. Source fields are strings.

node_common_properties._source_table: string; exact source table path, matching node_types[type].source_table
node_common_properties._source_row: positive integer; original CSV data-record index, excluding the header, not a physical line number

relation_common_fields.id: Unique deterministic string derived from source ID, relation type and target ID.
relation_common_fields.type: One of the 20 types declared in relations.
relation_common_fields.properties: Object containing required _join_rule and optional _admission_id_mismatch only.

relation_common_properties._join_rule: Required J-prefixed string matching a relations[].join_rule. J numbers follow the original 31-table join design, so gaps are expected; J02 and J04 each have multiple declarations distinguished by relationship and target type.
relation_common_properties._admission_id_mismatch: Optional boolean true when both endpoint hadm_id values are nonempty and differ. Absence does not establish admission identity when either value is missing.

value_semantics.storage: All original CSV properties remain strings, including numeric, date and identifier fields. Preserve whitespace, leading zeros, blank cells and duplicate source rows.
value_semantics.missing_values: An empty string retains a source blank. Its meaning is field-specific; for example, blank parent_field_ordinal identifies an event summary. Source property keys remain present. A blank is distinct from zero.
value_semantics.calculation: Numeric quantities and timestamps are stored as source strings; blanks and non-scalar text do not supply a numeric value. Identifiers are textual keys, and unit fields qualify quantities.
value_semantics.time: Dates are shifted with patient-specific offsets. This historical graph supplies no as_of or relation validity intervals. seq_num and source row order are not clinical event timestamps; chartdate has date-only precision.
value_semantics.scope: The selected source tables are retained for the four patients; dictionary rows are limited to referenced keys. This is not a complete record of all care. Other table identifiers remain properties without implied nodes or relationships.
value_semantics.joins: Each join_on field is nonempty and exactly equal at both endpoints. ICD joins include code and version. A pharmacy reference can retain disagreeing admission IDs; the mismatch flag records that source inconsistency.

Admission.meaning: One hospital admission, identified by hadm_id and linked to its patient by subject_id.
Admission.interpretation: admittime/dischtime delimit the hospital stay; edregtime/edouttime describe its emergency-department segment. deathtime and hospital_expire_flag concern in-hospital death. Repeated subject_id values represent separate admissions.

DiagnosisCode.meaning: A reusable ICD diagnosis definition, identified by the pair icd_code and icd_version.
DiagnosisCode.interpretation: long_title describes the code. Leading zeros and qualifiers such as history, with, without and unspecified are part of its meaning. Patient/admission assignments are represented by linked Diagnosis nodes.

ProcedureCode.meaning: A reusable ICD procedure definition, identified by the pair icd_code and icd_version.
ProcedureCode.interpretation: long_title describes the code. Patient/admission occurrences are represented by linked Procedure nodes; the dictionary itself has no patient or admission identifier.

LabItem.meaning: A laboratory test definition identified by itemid.
LabItem.interpretation: label names the test; fluid identifies specimen material; category groups tests. itemid links results to the test definition; display labels need not be unique. A LabItem is a concept, not a patient result.

Diagnosis.meaning: An ICD diagnosis assigned to a particular hospital admission for billing.
Diagnosis.interpretation: subject_id/hadm_id set the scope; seq_num is billing priority, not onset time. HAS_DIAGNOSIS_CODE supplies the description. Discharge coding does not establish when a condition became known or whether a history qualifier denotes an active condition.

MedAdmin.meaning: An eMAR medication event, identified by subject_id and emar_id.
MedAdmin.interpretation: charttime is the recorded event time, scheduletime its scheduled time, and storetime its documentation time. event_txt may indicate administration, delay or non-administration; the label alone does not prove a dose was given. Dose evidence is in HAS_DOSE_DETAIL. Missing hadm_id remains unassigned.

MedAdminDetail.meaning: A summary or component record belonging to one eMAR event; several rows can describe the same event.
MedAdminDetail.interpretation: Blank parent_field_ordinal identifies the event summary; populated ordinals identify components of that same event. dose_due/dose_due_unit describe intended dose, dose_given/dose_given_unit recorded dose, and product_amount_given/product_unit product quantity. pharmacy_id may differ across rows. Admission context is available through the parent MedAdmin when its hadm_id is present.

LabEvent.meaning: One laboratory result, identified by labevent_id; specimen_id can group multiple results from one specimen.
LabEvent.interpretation: value holds result text; valuenum holds its numeric representation when available, stored as a string here. valueuom and the reference-range fields qualify the result. charttime usually reflects specimen collection; storetime reflects result availability. A blank hadm_id does not identify the encounter type; this graph contains no admission links inferred from time.

Patient.meaning: One person identified by subject_id, with demographics and date-shifting anchors.
Patient.interpretation: anchor_age is age in anchor_year; 91 represents an age over 89 at that anchor. anchor_year_group maps the shifted anchor to a real-year range. dod is the recorded death date; a blank value does not prove survival.

PharmacyOrder.meaning: A medication-order record in the pharmacy system, identified by pharmacy_id.
PharmacyOrder.interpretation: medication, route, frequency, starttime/stoptime and status describe the order; entertime/verifiedtime describe its processing. FOR_PRESCRIPTION can reach multiple prescription rows. Administration events are recorded separately in MedAdmin. A flagged pharmacy reference records disagreeing admission IDs.

Prescription.meaning: A prescribed medication or order component; pharmacy_id is a linking field, not a unique prescription-row identifier.
Prescription.interpretation: drug_type distinguishes MAIN, BASE and ADDITIVE components. prod_strength is product composition; dose_val_rx/dose_unit_rx specify prescribed dose; doses_per_24_hrs gives frequency; route gives the intended route. starttime/stoptime describe the prescription period. Distinct source rows retain separate node IDs.

Procedure.meaning: An ICD procedure billed by the hospital for a particular admission.
Procedure.interpretation: subject_id/hadm_id set the scope; chartdate has date-only precision. seq_num is assigned priority and cannot establish within-day order. HAS_PROCEDURE_CODE supplies the description. These records cover hospital-billed procedures, not necessarily every procedure performed.

integrity_constraints: Node IDs and relation IDs are unique; every relation endpoint exists.
Every node has its declared source columns and the two common provenance properties; no source columns are renamed or removed.
Every relation matches exactly one declaration by _join_rule, type, source type and target type, and satisfies its exact nonempty join fields.
Each Diagnosis has exactly one HAS_DIAGNOSIS_CODE link to DiagnosisCode; each Procedure has exactly one HAS_PROCEDURE_CODE link to ProcedureCode; each LabEvent has exactly one MEASURES link.
Different source rows stay distinct even when their values or display names coincide.
